To print from your iPhone using AirPrint, follow these steps:

1. Make sure your iPhone and the AirPrint-enabled printer are connected to the same Wi-Fi network (iPhone User Guide, page 30).
2. From supported apps such as Mail, Photos, Safari, iBooks, Maps, or Notes, open the item you want to print.
3. Tap the Share icon ( or similar) or the action button within the app.
4. Choose the Print option.
5. Select your AirPrint-enabled printer.
6. Adjust print settings if needed, then tap Print.

For printing photos specifically:
- To print a single photo, tap the Share icon, then tap Print.
- To print multiple photos, open a photo album, tap Edit, select the photos, tap Share, then tap Print (iPhone User Guide, page 73).

For printing PDFs in iBooks:
- Open the PDF, tap the action button, then choose Print (iPhone User Guide, page 112).

For more details, see "Printing with AirPrint" on page 30 of the iPhone User Guide.

1. Hold down the Sleep/Wake button until the red slider appears.

3. To turn the iPhone back on, hold down the Sleep/Wake button until the Apple logo appears.

This procedure will restart your iPhone (iPhone User Guide, page 149 and page 8).

Personal Hotspot is a feature on iPhone 4 or later that allows you to share your iPhone's Internet connection with a computer or other devices such as an iPod touch, iPad, or another iPhone. Devices can connect to your iPhone's Internet via Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or USB. 

To use Personal Hotspot, you need:
1. An iPhone 4 or later.
2. Your iPhone must be connected to the Internet over the cellular data network.
3. You may need to set up the service with your carrier by going to Settings > General > Cellular and tapping Set Up Personal Hotspot if it appears.
4. Other devices can then connect to your iPhone via Wi-Fi by selecting your iPhone from the list of available Wi-Fi networks, via USB by connecting your iPhone to your computer with the cable, or via Bluetooth by turning on Bluetooth on your iPhone and pairing it with the device.

Note that this feature may not be available in all areas and additional fees may apply; you should contact your carrier for more information (iPhone User Guide, pages 132 and 135).

For example, you can say commands like "Call Joe," "Directions to the nearest Apple store," or "Is it going to rain tomorrow?" (iPhone User Guide, pages 36, 39).

To back up your iPhone with iCloud, follow these steps:

1. Go to Settings > iCloud.
2. Log in with your Apple ID and password, if required.
3. Go to Storage & Backup.
4. Turn on iCloud backups.

iCloud will back up your iPhone daily over Wi-Fi when it is connected to a power source and locked. It backs up purchased music, TV shows, apps, books, photos and videos in your Camera Roll, iPhone settings, app data, home screen and app organization, messages, and ringtones (iPhone User Guide, page 150).

Regarding backing up with iTunes, if you choose to back up using iCloud automatically, you cannot also use iTunes to automatically back up to your computer. However, you can still use iTunes to manually back up your iPhone to your computer (iPhone User Guide, page 150).

The difference between restarting and resetting your iPhone is as follows:

1. Restarting iPhone:
   - Hold down the Sleep/Wake button until the red slider appears.
   - Slide your finger across the slider to turn off iPhone.
   - To turn iPhone back on, hold down the Sleep/Wake button until the Apple logo appears.
   - Restarting is used to turn the device off and on again to resolve minor issues.

2. Resetting iPhone:
   - Should be done only if turning iPhone off and on doesn’t resolve the problem.
   - Hold down the Sleep/Wake button and the Home button at the same time for at least ten seconds, until the Apple logo appears.
   - Resetting forces a reboot and can help fix more persistent problems.

To force an app to close:
1. Hold down the Sleep/Wake button for a few seconds until a red slider appears.
2. Then hold down the Home button until the app closes.
3. Alternatively, you can remove an app from the recents list to force it to close (see Opening and switching between apps on page 17).

These instructions are from the iPhone User Guide, page 149.

To find your lost iPhone and protect your data, follow these steps:

1. Ensure that Find My iPhone was turned on in iCloud settings on your iPhone before it was lost. To turn it on, go to Settings > iCloud, then turn on Find My iPhone (iPhone User Guide, page 34).

2. Use the free Find My iPhone app on another iPhone, iPad, or iPod touch, or use a Mac or PC web browser signed in to www.icloud.com.

3. In the Find My iPhone app or on iCloud.com, you can:
   - Play Sound: Play a sound on your iPhone for two minutes to help locate it.
   - Lost Mode: Immediately lock your missing iPhone with a passcode and send it a message displaying a contact number. Your iPhone will also track and report its location.
   - Erase iPhone: Protect your privacy by erasing all the information and media on your iPhone and restoring it to its original factory settings (iPhone User Guide, page 34).

Important: Your iPhone must be connected to the Internet for these features to work (iPhone User Guide, page 34).

If your iPhone battery is dying too fast, consider the following steps based on the provided information:

1. Turn off 3G if you are making a lot of phone calls, as using 3G may decrease battery performance (iPhone User Guide, page 135).
2. Turn off Cellular Data for services you do not need to use cellular data with, so the iPhone will use only Wi-Fi for those services (iPhone User Guide, page 135).
3. Avoid using Data Roaming or Voice Roaming if not necessary, as these can increase battery usage (iPhone User Guide, page 135).
4. Make sure you are using the iPhone within the recommended operating temperature range (32° to 95° F or 0° to 35° C) because extreme temperatures can shorten battery life (iPhone User Guide, page 148).
5. If the battery is very old, it may have a limited number of charge cycles and might need to be replaced by an authorized service provider (iPhone User Guide, page 35).

Following these steps may help extend your iPhone's battery life. If problems persist, consider contacting Apple support for further assistance (iPhone User Guide, page 149).

To stop apps from knowing where you are, you need to turn off Location Services or restrict it for specific apps. Here are the steps:

1. Go to Settings > Privacy > Location Services.
2. You can turn off Location Services entirely by toggling it off, which stops all apps and services from accessing your location.
3. Alternatively, you can turn off Location Services for individual apps by selecting the app in the list and choosing "Never" or another option that restricts location access.
4. To turn off Location Services for system services, go to Settings > Privacy > Location Services > System Services and toggle off the services you want to restrict.

Note: If you turn off Location Services, you will be prompted to turn it on again the next time an app or service tries to use it (iPhone User Guide, page 140).

To stop your child from seeing explicit content or buying apps on your iPhone, follow these steps:

1. Turn on Restrictions:
   - Go to Settings > General > Restrictions.
   - Tap Enable Restrictions.
   - Define a restrictions passcode (different from the device unlock passcode).

2. Restrict explicit content:
   - Under Content Restrictions, tap Ratings For.
   - Select your country.
   - Set restrictions for music, podcasts, movies, TV shows, and apps so that content with explicit ratings won't appear on the iPhone.

3. Prevent app purchases:
   - Turn off In-App Purchases to prevent buying additional content or functionality within apps.
   - Enable Require Passwords to require entering your Apple ID for in-app purchases after a specified time period.

4. Disable installing and deleting apps:
   - Restrict Installing Apps to disable the App Store and remove its icon.
   - Restrict Deleting Apps to prevent apps from being deleted.

5. Restrict explicit language in Siri:
   - Enable the Explicit Language restriction so Siri replaces explicit words with asterisks and beep sounds.

These settings will help control explicit content visibility and prevent unauthorized app purchases (iPhone User Guide, page 137).

To fix a frozen iPhone that won't respond, follow these steps:

1. Try restarting the iPhone:
   - Hold down the Sleep/Wake button until the red slider appears.
   - Slide your finger across the slider to turn off the iPhone.
   - To turn it back on, hold down the Sleep/Wake button until the Apple logo appears.

2. If restarting doesn't work, try forcing an app to close:
   - Hold down the Sleep/Wake button for a few seconds until the red slider appears.
   - Then hold down the Home button until the app closes.

3. If you can’t turn off the iPhone or the problem continues, reset the iPhone:
   - Hold down the Sleep/Wake button and the Home button at the same time for at least ten seconds, until the Apple logo appears.

A reset should be done only if turning the iPhone off and on doesn’t resolve the problem (iPhone User Guide, pages 149).

To silence calls and notifications at night, you can use the Do Not Disturb feature by following these steps:

1. Go to Settings on your iPhone.
2. Turn on Do Not Disturb.
3. To schedule quiet hours, go to Settings > Notifications > Do Not Disturb.
4. Turn on Scheduled, then set the time when you don’t want to be disturbed. iPhone will automatically turn on Do Not Disturb during this period each day.
5. Optionally, you can allow calls from certain people to ring by tapping Allow Calls From and selecting your preferences.
6. When Do Not Disturb is on and the iPhone is locked, all notifications and calls are silenced, but alarms will still sound (iPhone User Guide, pages 10 and 132).

Alternatively, you can also flip the Ring/Silent switch on the side of your iPhone to silent mode, which stops the iPhone from ringing or playing alerts and other sound effects, though alarms and some app sounds will still play (iPhone User Guide, page 10).

To magnify the whole screen on your iPhone, follow these steps:

1. Go to Settings > General > Accessibility > Zoom.
2. Turn Zoom on.
3. To zoom in or out, double-tap the screen with three fingers.
4. To vary the magnification, with three fingers, tap and drag up or down without lifting your fingers on the second tap.
5. To pan around the screen while zoomed in, drag the screen with three fingers. After starting the drag, you can use a single finger to move around.

You can also turn Zoom on or off using the Triple-click Home function (Settings > General > Accessibility > Triple-click Home) (iPhone User Guide, page 125).

To charge your iPhone from a wall outlet, follow these steps:

1. Use the included USB cable (Lightning to USB Cable for iPhone 5 or later, or 30-pin to USB Cable for iPhone 4S or earlier).
2. Connect the USB end of the cable to the Apple USB power adapter.
3. Plug the power adapter into a power outlet.
4. Connect the other end of the cable to your iPhone.
5. Make sure the AC plug or AC power cord is fully inserted into the adapter before plugging it into the power outlet.
6. Allow adequate ventilation around the power adapter during use, as it may become warm.
7. Avoid using damaged cables or chargers, and do not charge when moisture is present to prevent electric shock.

Note: In some regions, you may need an iPhone Micro USB Adapter to connect to certain power adapters. Only use power adapters compliant with specified standards or "Made for iPhone" cables and adapters compatible with USB 2.0 (iPhone User Guide, pages 8, 34, 147).
